items.summary: Recent video-based world models pair the scalability of autoregressive (AR) prediction with the visual quality of diffusion models. The choice of scene tokenizer is paramount for the optimal performance of each of these, both in terms of fidelity and semantics. Flexible-length, coarse-to-fine tokenizers yield exactly that: the first coarse tokens carry the clip's global semantics while later tokens further specify details. Existing flexible tokenizers only apply a representation-alignment (REPA) loss on early decoder hidden states, a target the decoder can partly meet from its noised input instead. We introduce SemanTok, a flexible video tokenizer that feeds frozen DINO features into its encoder and adds lightweight heads that reconstruct them from each retained token prefix alone. SemanTok achieves high semantic alignment and video fidelity at every AR model size: a 201M SemanTok AR model matches or beats a VideoFlexTok AR model $3.4\times$ its size, and larger SemanTok AR models further improve fidelity. It keeps semantic alignment on out-of-distribution classes and gives the decoder higher semantic alignment at every noise level, including pure noise. It performs well in both reconstruction and generation, and its short token prefixes are cheaper to predict and give better generation fidelity, with pixel detail deferred to later tokens.
items.title: SemanTok: Predictable Semantic Tokens for Efficient Autoregressive Video Generation

items.summary: World models allow agents to plan in latent space by choosing a sequence of actions that most reduces the distance to a given goal state. Thus, planning can benefit from latent representations whose distances mirror commute-times in the environment. The spectral embedding space of the graph Laplacian provides such a representation, if it obeys a specific eigenvalue-dependent scaling. Unfortunately, instantiating the graph Laplacian is intractable in large, continuous environments. Self-supervised learning offers a natural route to such commute-time-preserving embeddings at scale. However, here we show that existing methods, which commonly encourage isotropic representations to prevent representational collapse, tend to degrade the "correct" eigenvalue-dependent scaling, leading to an inaccurate representation of commute times. To address this problem, we introduce Commute-Time-Preserving World Models (CTWMs), combining a latent displacement predictor and a log-determinant regularizer that prevents collapse, which provably recover the correctly scaled Laplacian representation under reversible deterministic dynamics and at the predictor's fixed point. In numerical simulations, CTWM matches or outperforms LeWM, a task-agnostic baseline, on several complex, continuous goal-reaching benchmarks, while using half the parameters.
items.title: Learning Commute-Time-Preserving World Models for Planning

items.summary: This record provides the reproducibility package accompanying the study " Resolving BTEX Mixtures under Infrared Spectral Interference with Dual-Representation Learning." The archive contains frozen author-generated BTEX training, validation, test, and composition-held-out Challenge datasets; final model configurations and random seeds; trained model checkpoints; and source code for spectral simulation, model training and evaluation, representation analysis, Integrated Gradients analysis, hyperparameter optimization, statistical analysis, and external spectral transfer. It also includes audit records for the final hyperparameter-optimization studies and paired-bootstrap analysis, together with provenance information for the external spectral resources used in the study. Raw third-party HITRAN/PNNL, NIST, and U.S. EPA infrared spectra and derived source templates with unconfirmed redistribution rights are not redistributed. Source identifiers, acquisition information, checksums, and preprocessing provenance are provided to support independent retrieval from the original sources.
items.title: Reproducibility Package for Resolving BTEX Mixtures under Infrared Spectral Interference with Dual-Representation Learning

items.summary: Abstract   The Universal Research System with Reverse Itinerary (SUII) is a retrospective analytical methodology designed to reconstruct, in a traceable and auditable manner, the probable pathway leading from an initial problem or question to a completed scientific product. This manual brings together the universal prompt, a mandatory common core, ten core modules—including bibliographic analysis (SUII-B)—and six specialised extensions: journalistic and opinion texts (SUII-P), audiovisual or audio documents (SUII-AV), legislation and regulatory documents (SUII-L), case law and judicial decisions (SUII-J), critical appraisal of scientific articles (SUII-LC), and traceable research information management for datasets and research data objects (SUII-TRIM). Each module guides the extraction of locatable traces, classification of the epistemic status of claims, and construction of matrices linking evidence, inference, confidence, alternatives, and required verification. SUII-TRIM extends this logic to the provenance, versioning, transformation, quality control, preservation, access, and reuse of research datasets, while preserving the distinction between directly observed information, information provided by the researcher, reasoned inference, and non-determinable information. The method separates retrospective reconstruction from the prospective generation of hypotheses and requires rival explanations whenever the evidence does not support a unique conclusion. It also incorporates procedures for methodological auditing, version comparison, conceptual genealogy, peer review, algorithmic-bias assessment, external validation, teaching, and traceable research data management. SUII is not intended to recover the authors’ actual psychological history or to replace validated tools for methodological appraisal, risk-of-bias assessment, certainty of evidence, data stewardship, or repository curation. Its application requires version-controlled corpora, decision logs, retention of prompts and outputs, source verification, preservation of original data objects when applicable, and mandatory human oversight. When the available traces are insufficient, the appropriate result is “not determinable.” The manual provides practical criteria for selecting, combining, and quality-controlling the modules according to the product under analysis and the research objective, while maintaining explicit boundaries between documented evidence, reasoned inference, speculation, and unresolved uncertainty .   Resumen   El Sistema Universal de Investigación con Itinerario Inverso (SUII) es una metodología de análisis retrospectivo orientada a reconstruir, de forma trazable y auditable, el itinerario probable que conduce desde un problema o pregunta inicial hasta un producto científico finalizado. Este manual reúne el prompt universal, un núcleo común obligatorio, diez módulos nucleares y seis extensiones especializadas: análisis bibliográfico (SUII-B), textos periodísticos y de opinión (SUII-P), documentos audiovisuales o sonoros (SUII-AV), legislación y normativa (SUII-L), jurisprudencia y sentencias (SUII-J), lectura crítica de artículos científicos (SUII-LC) y gestión trazable de información y datos de investigación (SUII-TRIM). Cada módulo guía la extracción de huellas localizables, la clasificación del estado epistemológico de las afirmaciones y la construcción de matrices que relacionan evidencia, inferencia, confianza, alternativas y comprobaciones necesarias. El método separa la reconstrucción retrospectiva de la generación prospectiva de hipótesis y exige formular explicaciones rivales cuando la evidencia no permite una conclusión única. Asimismo, incorpora procedimientos para auditoría me

items.summary: Classical metaphysics treats the mutual exclusivity of alternatives as primitive: or, in its physical reading, excludes by nature. This paper argues the polarity should be reversed. Exclusivity is an achievement — stated, interior, structural content of the alternatives them-selves — rather than an intrinsic feature of disjunction; and once exclusion is relocated from the exterior of or to interior content, a new composition regime falls out with no further postulation: the joint regime, in which co-present alternatives simply decline to carry mu-tual negations. The difference between the regimes is fixed by a one-statement test, which answers the suspicion of mere notation; a strict fence separates what the new primitive sup-plies (openness) from anything its occupants might do with it (use), which blocks the two natural misreadings; and the primitive itself receives a deflationary definition: or-jointness is the logic-valued regime of not stating mutual negations on the interior side — obtained by declension, not addition. We argue the proposal reclassifies the color-exclusion problem that fractured the Tractatus, and supplies the determinable-based literature on metaphysical indeterminacy with the composition story it has lacked. A documented fact about the direction of discovery then bears on the proposal’s status: the two composition forms were first extracted, in companion work, from the case-by-case structure of interference phenomena — before the present philosophy existed — so the dichotomy’s shape is explained by what it was extracted from, not by any philosophical purpose it might serve. Whether the world instantiates the joint regime is the companion framework’s proposal, on which no thesis here leans; what the provenance establishes is that the primitive was not gerrymandered for the argument that now exposes it.
items.title: Exclusivity as Achievement: Relocating Mutual Exclusion to the Interior, and the Logical Primitive That Falls Out

items.summary: The laws of physics are CPT-symmetric, yet laboratory quantum mechanics prepares the past and only samples the future. This working paper distinguishes five levels of taking the symmetry seriously — symmetric laws with the open future left implicit, a two-boundary description, symmetric processes, a nontrivial final boundary, and laboratory access to it — places published views and experiments on them, and states what each predicts for a final-boundary test, in which an engineered terminal acts on a flag and an entangled partner is read on every trial. Exact results: an open future propagates backward through any physical channel; a terminal can only transfer, never manufacture, final-side contrast, giving lambda = tanh(hbar omega / 2 k T_f) in a swap model, the mirror of a reset; a clamp of budget A needs an energy of at least k T_f ln A in some branch; under free local control any every-trial final condition signals, with visibility equal to the clamp strength. Under stated transfer models a null reads as a lower bound on a swap-equivalent final temperature (Partridge: above 3.5e7 K for escaping microwaves; planned qubit tests: about 27 K and 360 K). The paper audits transport to the future, specifies what any physical source of a final condition must supply, and finds that no named candidate meets the specification. CPT motivates the reversed-resource question; channel duality bounds its possible transfer; laboratory access remains an additional physical hypothesis, decided only by experiment. No new experimental result is reported. Drafted with AI assistance and revised after AI-assisted reviews; responsibility rests with the author.
tags: CPT symmetry; arrow of time; two-boundary quantum mechanics, final boundary condition; absorber theory; Landauer principle; postselection; no-signalling; two-way quantum computing
items.title: How seriously do we take CPT? Levels of time-symmetry acceptance, and what each predicts for final-boundary tests and two-way quantum computing

items.summary: Berggren's three matrices generate the tree of primitive Pythagorean triples and preserve the quadratic form x₁² + x₂² − x₃². Cha, Nguyen and Tauber (2018) built such trees for other integral ternary forms Q of signature (2,1). We ask whether the matrices alone determine Q. Main results: Recovery criterion (Theorem 3.1). A set of isometries of Q determines Q up to scale exactly when no nonzero vector is sent to plus or minus itself by all of them. Equivalently, the group they generate is not virtually abelian; for integral isometries, it acts irreducibly. The proof is elementary linear algebra and applies to arbitrary real groups. Berggren trees (Theorem 3.2, Proposition 3.3, Remark 3.5). Any two generators determine Q in Berggren's tree and in each of the five trees of Cha, Nguyen and Tauber. The definition of a Berggren tree alone does not force this: the generators A and A² give a Berggren forest for x₁² + x₂² − x₃² whose two generators both yield edges but do not determine Q. Roots at a rational null line (Theorem 3.6). For a primitive null vector P with divisor G, the minimum of Q on (P^⊥ ∩ ℤ³) \ ℤP is S = |det(2J)|/(2G²). An explicit congruence, Gm ≡ −τ (mod S), decides which minimal vectors e + mP are roots. N-cusps (Theorems 3.7–3.8, Corollary 3.9). For Q = ax₁² + bx₁x₂ + cx₂² − Nx₃² with D = b² − 4ac < 0, all data at the null vectors (p, q, 1) are explicit. A minimal root exists there if and only if gcd(G, S) divides D/G, and in particular whenever D is cube-free. Recovery by integral reflections (Theorem 3.12, Proposition 3.13). Minimal roots at two or three distinct rational null lines yield three integral reflections that determine Q. The paper also relates the reflections in the trees of Cha, Nguyen and Tauber to minimal roots (Remark 3.17), and states an open question for trees produced by their construction.
items.title: The Inverse Berggren Tree Problem

items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly construct multi-agent workflows that decompose a complex task and assign specialist agents from a pool. However, building such a workflow well remains challenging: how finely to divide the task, which agent to trust with each subtask, and when to create a new specialist are all critical decisions a workflow constructor needs to settle up front. Thus, whether each subtask succeeds remains unknown until the workflow runs. Yet, improving a workflow is costly. Locating a fault usually requires a reference answer, a graded outcome, or a trained assessor, and the fix is applied to the whole workflow through re-execution, re-search, or retraining. We propose InFlowOp, which prices every decision in one label-free cost that weighs how well an agent's competence meets what a subtask demands against how much that agent takes to run. Before execution, InFlowOp bidirectionally determines the granularity of task decomposition and agent assignment following from the cost rather than from a fixed template. During execution, InFlowOp corrects a fault with the cheapest move via the same cost that serves the workflow both as it is built and as it runs. Facing the workflow-level evaluation challenge, we introduce Braid, a benchmark whose tasks require multi-agent coordination beyond single-agent capability. Across various domains and backbones, InFlowOp outperforms single agent baselines by up to $+11.97\%$, achieving $+9.64\%$ with in-flow optimization. Our project page: https://xhguo7.github.io/InFlowOp/.
items.title: Pay for the Fault, Not the Flow: Label-Free In-Flow Multi-Agent Workflow Optimization
Observational rheological bounds for Antarctic ice shelves from inverse modelling under Glen's n = 4 flow law

items.summary: Controlling an agent with vision requires being able to separate useful information from irrelevant background information. JEPA-style latent world models seem like a natural approach for this, as they do not perform pixel-level reconstruction; however, they are still sensitive to these distractor signals and experience latent collapse. In this work, we introduce Controllability Factorized JEPA (CF-JEPA), a JEPA-style world model which splits the latent space into controllable and uncontrollable subspaces. This factorization allows us to capture all the distractor information into the uncontrollable region, while we use the control-relevant latent information for our task. With this, we show comparable performance across 2D and 3D control tasks under nominal conditions and improved performance under distracted conditions, where CF-JEPA is the only model that does not experience latent collapse. We also validate our model under distracted conditions for a simulated robot task, highlighting the practical application of such a scheme.
items.title: CF-JEPA: Improving Robustness of JEPA World Models via Controllability Factorization

items.summary: A time series world model (TSWM) predicts a controlled system's state from its observed history and planned actions and exogenous inputs. Current approaches build forecasters with actions as covariates, trained and evaluated on prediction error under the executed plan. Yet world models compare unexecuted plans, but their responses to changed plans remain untested. We ask which design choices matter and whether accurate forecasters respond to changed plans as real systems do. We address both with a formalization and benchmark. The formalization separates state, actions and exogenous inputs, distinguishes continuous, mode and event actions, and introduces mechanism consistency, a metric built on declared action-state relations with known directions, such as a vasopressor raising blood pressure: it checks whether shifting an action moves the forecast in the declared direction. The benchmark consolidates eight public datasets with real actions from engineered infrastructure and clinical care, varying prediction space, plan fusion and plan encoding across seven backbones and five seeds. First, a frozen latent prediction space lowers MAE by 9.9% over observation space and gated output fusion lowers it by 12.7% over input concatenation on average, with both improving all eight datasets; temporal plan encoding changes average MAE by at most 2.2%. Second, prediction error and mechanism consistency diverge: the lowest-error configuration is at or below chance in consistency on four of five datasets with declared mechanisms, and no design choice avoids this. Finally, directional supervision, a loss penalizing the wrong-signed part of the response to a shifted action, significantly raises consistency on penalized mechanisms with no change in MAE. Together they give TSWMs a recipe: a frozen latent space and output-side fusion for accuracy, and a training objective for mechanism consistency.
items.title: On the Divergence of Accuracy and Mechanism Consistency in Time Series World Models

items.summary: This repository provides the compiled analysis inputs, R code, figure source data and GIS rasters supporting the manuscript “Historical introduction pools pre-structure future plant invasion debt under climate change”. Version 2.0 contains the final USA-intersection climatic-analogue reconstruction and its corresponding model predictions and spatial summaries. The historical introduction pool contains 18,562 species. The stage-transition models use 5,791 complete-case species, of which 4,088 species without a recorded invasion form the future candidate invasion-debt subset. Future predictions cover 12 combinations of two climate scenarios (SSP126 and SSP585), three periods (2041–2060, 2061–2080 and 2081–2100), and two global climate models (HadGEM3-GC31-LL and MPI-ESM1-2-HR). The archive contains: • Figure_data: XLSX source workbooks for main Figures 1–4, Supplementary Figures S1–S4 and Supplementary Tables S1–S15, together with the compiled species-level analysis dataset and current and future candidate-species predictions. • Code: R scripts, computational inputs and provenance documentation for the stage-transition models, climatic-analogue searches, future predictions, phylogenetic null analysis, temporal analyses, sensitivity analyses and publication source tables. • GIS_rasters: GeoTIFFs for the main and supplementary spatial figures. Main Figure 4 rasters contain sums within globally aligned 0.5° display cells; supplementary spatial rasters retain the native 10-arc-minute resolution. • Validation: execution records and numerical checks. • README files: instructions for reproducing the analyses, plotting the source data and interpreting the spatial fields. Current and future closest US climatic analogue cells are identified separately for each candidate species. POT is the sum of future predicted invasion probabilities assigned to future analogue cells. CHG is future grid-level transition potential minus current grid-level transition potential, with unassigned cells completed with zero. CHG therefore incorporates both changes in predicted probability and relocation of climatic analogues. POSDP is the sum of positive species-level changes assigned to future analogue cells; Supplementary Figure S3 reports its range across the two climate models. The analytical workflow was tested with R 4.3.3. Reproduction starts from the compiled historical master dataset, supplied phylogenetic inputs, prepared species climatic centroids and extracted WorldClim grid values. The package does not independently repeat every upstream archive-curation decision, manual stage-status assignment, GBIF download or occurrence-cleaning step. These boundaries and the optional XLSX and GeoTIFF export procedures are documented in the README. The historical count of 15,950 candidate invasion-debt species is retained for historical summaries; it is not the population used for future predictions. This release supersedes the earlier spatial outputs based on a rectangular climate-search domain. Future results should be interpreted as conditional model projections rather than evidence of a statistically established climate-driven increase in invasion. items.summary: The Olist Transactional Evidence Benchmark (OTEB) is a neutral, derived research dataset for evaluating analytical methods under incomplete, conflicting, ambiguous, and reconstructable transactional evidence. OTEB is derived from the Brazilian E-Commerce Public Dataset by Olist . It provides a frozen reference cohort of 94,791 internally reconciled orders, 901 deterministic controlled instances, transaction-instance membership, evaluator-only oracle states, and state-specific monetary exposure. The benchmark represents four evidence states: `CONFIRMED`, `RECONSTRUCTED`, `CONFLICTING`, and `UNRESOLVED`. Controlled families cover missing evidence, hard conflicts, unique reconstruction, ambiguous reconstruction, duplicate evidence, and mixed corruption at 5%, 10%, 20%, 30%, and 40%. This release contains the reference oracle, controlled-instance definitions, compact membership index, exposure tables, data dictionary, provenance documentation, reconstruction code, validation code, manifests, schema catalog, and checksums. It contains no method predictions, comparative performance results, ablation studies, paper drafts, dashboards, or private Rahaskin data. Raw Olist CSV files are not redistributed and must be obtained from the original Kaggle source. Original source citation: Olist, & Sionek, A. (2018). Brazilian E-Commerce Public Dataset by Olist [Data set]. Kaggle. https://doi.org/10.34740/KAGGLE/DSV/195341 Official source: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/olistbr/brazilian-ecommerce License: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International (`CC BY-NC-SA 4.0`).

items.summary: GradLint is a fast, standalone Rust-based command-line tool and Python package for diffusion MRI gradient-table quality control. It audits FSL and MRtrix gradient schemes, detects b-vector flip and axis-permutation errors using DWI image evidence, and writes corrected gradient tables with machine-readable provenance. GradLint is designed as a QC gate before diffusion MRI preprocessing, reconstruction, or tractography pipelines. It checks whether the supplied gradient table is geometrically consistent with the diffusion image, reports scheme-quality issues such as shell structure, direction counts, b0 handling, non-unit b-vectors, and angular sampling, and identifies silent convention errors that can otherwise propagate into tensor fitting and tractography results. The core detection method ranks signed axis permutations of the gradient table by a fibre-coherence criterion derived from a diffusion tensor fit. Candidate conventions are evaluated in the appropriate image or world frame for the input format: FSL bvec/bval tables are treated as image-relative, while MRtrix .b tables are treated as world-coordinate gradients. When a high-confidence correction is found, GradLint can emit repaired FSL and/or MRtrix gradient files together with JSON provenance describing the decision, transform, inputs, and outputs.  The software is implemented as a Rust core with thin command-line and Python interfaces. The Python package exposes the same functionality as the CLI and can render JSON reports to Markdown or HTML. Input gradient files are never modified in place unless an explicit overwrite option is used. This record archives the source code for GradLint v1.1.6, corresponding to the GitHub release published on 2026-10-03. The archived source includes the Rust core, CLI, Python bindings, report rendering layer, tests, CI/release metadata, and example materials included in the public source tree. Repository: https://github.com/marcotag93/GradLint Release: https://github.com/marcotag93/GradLint/releases/tag/v1.1.6 PyPI: https://pypi.org/project/gradlint/ Concept DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20847595

The method separates retrospective reconstruction from the prospective generation of hypotheses and requires rival explanations whenever the evidence does not support a unique conclusion. It also incorporates procedures for methodological auditing, version comparison, conceptual genealogy, peer review, algorithmic-bias assessment, external validation, teaching, and traceable research data management. items.summary: Classical metaphysics treats the mutual exclusivity of alternatives as primitive: or, in its physical reading, excludes by nature. This paper argues the polarity should be reversed. Exclusivity is an achievement — stated, interior, structural content of the alternatives them-selves — rather than an intrinsic feature of disjunction; and once exclusion is relocated from the exterior of or to interior content, a new composition regime falls out with no further postulation: the joint regime, in which co-present alternatives simply decline to carry mu-tual negations. The difference between the regimes is fixed by a one-statement test, which answers the suspicion of mere notation; a strict fence separates what the new primitive sup-plies (openness) from anything its occupants might do with it (use), which blocks the two natural misreadings; and the primitive itself receives a deflationary definition: or-jointness is the logic-valued regime of not stating mutual negations on the interior side — obtained by declension, not addition. We argue the proposal reclassifies the color-exclusion problem that fractured the Tractatus, and supplies the determinable-based literature on metaphysical indeterminacy with the composition story it has lacked. A documented fact about the direction of discovery then bears on the proposal’s status: the two composition forms were first extracted, in companion work, from the case-by-case structure of interference phenomena — before the present philosophy existed — so the dichotomy’s shape is explained by what it was extracted from, not by any philosophical purpose it might serve. Whether the world instantiates the joint regime is the companion framework’s proposal, on which no thesis here leans; what the provenance establishes is that the primitive was not gerrymandered for the argument that now exposes it.
items.title: Exclusivity as Achievement: Relocating Mutual Exclusion to the Interior, and the Logical Primitive That Falls Out

items.summary: This chapter develops the research programme of Generative Relational Economics (GRE) by translating the conceptual, methodological, and substantive architectures developed earlier in the book into a cumulative, contestable, and revisable programme of inquiry. Its principal concern is answerability: GRE claims should specify what is being investigated, what kinds of evidence can support them, what would count against them, which methods are appropriate to their objects, and under what conditions their scope, formulation, or status should change. The chapter first distinguishes the epistemic status of GRE claims and establishes a modular research architecture. It then formulates research programmes for relational economic structures, allocation, heterogeneous value, value conversion and circulation, generative return, generative spacetime, fast–slow dynamics, economic power, justice, generative exploitation, epistemic economy, and AI-mediated capability asymmetry. These substantive programmes are complemented by domain studies, formal modelling, historical and interpretive inquiry, quantitative and empirical research, comparative theory, institutional experimentation, measurement analysis, counterevidence, negative results, replication, reinterpretation, and research infrastructure. A recurring concern is to prevent operationalization from collapsing the distinctions that motivate GRE. Measurement is therefore treated as a transformation with possible loss and reflexive effects; formalization is treated as task-relative rather than as evidence of ontological commitment; justice research keeps normative premises explicit; power and exploitation require mechanism-level identification rather than inference from asymmetry alone; and cross-domain translation preserves non-equivalence and domain-specific remainders. Failed models, failed translations, null results, counterexamples, and negative evidence are treated as constitutive resources for cumulative research rather than as residuals to be discarded. The chapter concludes by specifying how GRE may interact with neighboring Generative Relational domains while retaining disciplinary containment. Candidate cross-domain structures remain hypotheses for further inquiry rather than presumptive components of a completed general theory. GRE thereby emerges not as a closed theoretical system, but as an open research programme whose concepts, methods, models, and domain claims remain historically situated, empirically answerable, formally inspectable, and institutionally revisable.
items.title: Generative Relational Economics - Chapter 22: Research Programme of Generative Relational Economics

items.summary: Sunnycode v1 provides an open-access computational framework and reproducibility package supporting the research article Failure-Aware Gateway Placement and Road-Constrained Backbone Optimization for Resilient Urban LoRaWAN Networks , submitted to Digital Communications and Networks. The framework integrates OpenStreetMap (OSM) building-level sensing demand, radio-frequency (RF) feasibility, capacity-aware gateway assignment, worst-case single-gateway failure retention (N−1), gateway-load fairness, and road-constrained Steiner backbone synthesis. The repository includes Python implementations of the proposed optimization approach and four independent benchmark methods (Genetic Algorithm, Particle Swarm Optimization, Greedy, and Random Search). Dataset and experimental scope The computational experiment considers 685 building-level sensor anchors, 169 road vertices, 195 street edges, and 89 gateway candidates. The Full benchmark comprises 4,000 run-level observations obtained from 100 repetitions for each combination of five optimization methods and eight gateway budgets (k = 3–10). Repository contents Python source code and computational validation utilities. Nine original CSV files containing experimental observations, aggregated statistics, evaluation effort, and optimizer provenance. OpenStreetMap territorial input ( sunny3.osm ). Forty scientific figures in PDF format. Installation and execution instructions using Anaconda. SHA-256 file-integrity manifest and licensing information. The archived results support independent verification of the reported statistics and new computational experiments. The original historical environment metadata and detailed event histories are not included; therefore, bit-for-bit replay of the historical execution environment is not claimed. Scientific scope: RF coverage and packet delivery ratio are model-derived planning estimates rather than field-calibrated measurements. N−1 resilience represents gateway-access service retention and does not certify fault-tolerant physical-backbone connectivity. This software and dataset are released to support transparent computational research, independent assessment, and further development of resilient urban Internet of Things infrastructure planning.
items.title: Sunnycode v1 A Reproducible Framework for Failure-Aware Gateway Placement and Road-Constrained Backbone Optimization in Urban LoRaWAN Networks

items.summary: End-to-end research agents can now produce complete scientific papers, yet manuscript claims often diverge from executed experiments. This gap is structural: research state, failure histories, and claim-evidence alignment are not maintained as persistent, verifiable state across long-horizon pipelines. We present YouRA (Your Research Agent), an architecture for stateful, evidence-traceable autonomous research. YouRA preserves research state, execution evidence, and failure history across the research trajectory by integrating three components: a Verification State Architecture (VSA) that tracks hypotheses, gates, and evidence pointers; an Independent Controller that turns state and reflection records into lifecycle, recovery, and debate/review control while separating control from execution; and Stateful Reflection that logs failures as structured lessons and routes recovery through bounded repair, redesign, or reset. On MLR-Bench's predefined ten-task end-to-end subset, YouRA improves over both MLR-Agent and AI Scientist V2 on scalar Overall across all three matched backbones. An automated diagnostic using MLR-Bench's hallucination taxonomy reports intersection/union counts for four fact-based failure types, and data-provenance diagnostic shows more real-data-based outputs. Ablating each of the four components (the VSA, the Independent Controller, MCP tool access, and reflection-guided recovery) supports their separable contributions. Removing either core-state component drops YouRA below the full system. Code: https://github.com/PrayPrey/Your-Research-Agent.
items.title: YouRA: A Persistent-State Architecture for Evidence-Traceable Autonomous Research Agents

Scientific text recovery retains source evidence for signs, units, exponents, Chinese encoding and overlapping accent glyphs (#303, #306, #316). Preparation receipts reach scratch extraction, and stale receipts retire when the producer changes. Treatment headings require explicit taxonomic authority syntax; global sections clear prior species context. Served source provenance uses bounded previews with explicit truncation and evidence counts (#319). items.summary: Privacy-derived scientific materials for controlled studies of evidence access and adverse product content in AI assessment. The supplement contains synthetic materials, prompts, recorded model answers, terminal failures, assignment mappings, original stage-specific scoring and statistical implementations, reference results, and an offline CPU replay entrypoint. It includes the main local studies, the hosted-model study, historical screening, two common-interface qualification rounds, and the exploratory two-model pilot. Screening and development records are kept distinct from formal comparisons; reused answer aliases are not independent generations. The qualification amendment was made after qualification and before the exploratory pilot, and the subsequent proposed formal extension was not run. The findings do not establish a general advantage of pre-event defense, equivalence, or broad robustness. This is a redacted scientific derivative with a new integrity manifest: account authorizations, user dialogue, machine paths, hardware logs, original provider envelopes, encrypted reasoning, native token journals and model weights are excluded. CPU replay reproduces scores and statistics from the released scientific records; it does not regenerate answers or repeat the original private token/authorization/environment audits.
items.title: Scientific supplement for Evidence Access and Adverse Product Content in AI Assessment

items.summary: Recent video-based world models pair the scalability of autoregressive (AR) prediction with the visual quality of diffusion models. The choice of scene tokenizer is paramount for the optimal performance of each of these, both in terms of fidelity and semantics. Flexible-length, coarse-to-fine tokenizers yield exactly that: the first coarse tokens carry the clip's global semantics while later tokens further specify details. Existing flexible tokenizers only apply a representation-alignment (REPA) loss on early decoder hidden states, a target the decoder can partly meet from its noised input instead. We introduce SemanTok, a flexible video tokenizer that feeds frozen DINO features into its encoder and adds lightweight heads that reconstruct them from each retained token prefix alone. SemanTok achieves high semantic alignment and video fidelity at every AR model size: a 201M SemanTok AR model matches or beats a VideoFlexTok AR model $3.4\times$ its size, and larger SemanTok AR models further improve fidelity. It keeps semantic alignment on out-of-distribution classes and gives the decoder higher semantic alignment at every noise level, including pure noise. It performs well in both reconstruction and generation, and its short token prefixes are cheaper to predict and give better generation fidelity, with pixel detail deferred to later tokens.
items.title: SemanTok: Predictable Semantic Tokens for Efficient Autoregressive Video Generation

items.summary: World models allow agents to plan in latent space by choosing a sequence of actions that most reduces the distance to a given goal state. Thus, planning can benefit from latent representations whose distances mirror commute-times in the environment. The spectral embedding space of the graph Laplacian provides such a representation, if it obeys a specific eigenvalue-dependent scaling. Unfortunately, instantiating the graph Laplacian is intractable in large, continuous environments. Self-supervised learning offers a natural route to such commute-time-preserving embeddings at scale. However, here we show that existing methods, which commonly encourage isotropic representations to prevent representational collapse, tend to degrade the "correct" eigenvalue-dependent scaling, leading to an inaccurate representation of commute times. To address this problem, we introduce Commute-Time-Preserving World Models (CTWMs), combining a latent displacement predictor and a log-determinant regularizer that prevents collapse, which provably recover the correctly scaled Laplacian representation under reversible deterministic dynamics and at the predictor's fixed point. In numerical simulations, CTWM matches or outperforms LeWM, a task-agnostic baseline, on several complex, continuous goal-reaching benchmarks, while using half the parameters.
items.title: Learning Commute-Time-Preserving World Models for Planning

items.summary: This record provides the reproducibility package accompanying the study " Resolving BTEX Mixtures under Infrared Spectral Interference with Dual-Representation Learning." The archive contains frozen author-generated BTEX training, validation, test, and composition-held-out Challenge datasets; final model configurations and random seeds; trained model checkpoints; and source code for spectral simulation, model training and evaluation, representation analysis, Integrated Gradients analysis, hyperparameter optimization, statistical analysis, and external spectral transfer. It also includes audit records for the final hyperparameter-optimization studies and paired-bootstrap analysis, together with provenance information for the external spectral resources used in the study. Raw third-party HITRAN/PNNL, NIST, and U.S. EPA infrared spectra and derived source templates with unconfirmed redistribution rights are not redistributed. Source identifiers, acquisition information, checksums, and preprocessing provenance are provided to support independent retrieval from the original sources.
items.title: Reproducibility Package for Resolving BTEX Mixtures under Infrared Spectral Interference with Dual-Representation Learning

The materials cover the paired clean-versus-clean harm calibration, the Stage 1 policy-development analysis, the Stage 2 confirmation analysis, all five prespecified operating profiles, policy selection and multiplicity analyses, baseline comparisons, broadened fault analyses, model-family validation, native Great Expectations validation, harm-threshold sensitivity, provenance and transfer audits, and supporting consistency checks. The package is organised using descriptive file names and is intended to permit independent inspection and reproduction of the reported computational results. The accompanying article defines the experimental protocol, scope of the empirical certificates, statistical interpretation, and limitations of the study.

items.summary: World models allow agents to plan in latent space by choosing a sequence of actions that most reduces the distance to a given goal state. Thus, planning can benefit from latent representations whose distances mirror commute-times in the environment. The spectral embedding space of the graph Laplacian provides such a representation, if it obeys a specific eigenvalue-dependent scaling. Unfortunately, instantiating the graph Laplacian is intractable in large, continuous environments. Self-supervised learning offers a natural route to such commute-time-preserving embeddings at scale. However, here we show that existing methods, which commonly encourage isotropic representations to prevent representational collapse, tend to degrade the "correct" eigenvalue-dependent scaling, leading to an inaccurate representation of commute times. To address this problem, we introduce Commute-Time-Preserving World Models (CTWMs), combining a latent displacement predictor and a log-determinant regularizer that prevents collapse, which provably recover the correctly scaled Laplacian representation under reversible deterministic dynamics and at the predictor's fixed point. In numerical simulations, CTWM matches or outperforms LeWM, a task-agnostic baseline, on several complex, continuous goal-reaching benchmarks, while using half the parameters.
items.title: Learning Commute-Time-Preserving World Models for Planning

items.summary: This record contains the replication package accompanying the article “DCMT-Cert: Empirical Adequacy Certification of Machine-Learning Data-Contract Gates.” The package provides the scripts, retained numerical outputs, analysis tables, audit materials, dataset manifests, source hashes, and checksum information required to reproduce and inspect the computational analyses reported in the article. The materials cover the paired clean-versus-clean harm calibration, the Stage 1 policy-development analysis, the Stage 2 confirmation analysis, all five prespecified operating profiles, policy selection and multiplicity analyses, baseline comparisons, broadened fault analyses, model-family validation, native Great Expectations validation, harm-threshold sensitivity, provenance and transfer audits, and supporting consistency checks. The package is organised using descriptive file names and is intended to permit independent inspection and reproduction of the reported computational results. The accompanying article defines the experimental protocol, scope of the empirical certificates, statistical interpretation, and limitations of the study.
items.title: Replication Package for "DCMT-Cert: Empirical Adequacy Certification of Machine-Learning Data-Contract Gates"

items.summary: The Olist Transactional Evidence Benchmark (OTEB) is a neutral, derived research dataset for evaluating analytical methods under incomplete, conflicting, ambiguous, and reconstructable transactional evidence. OTEB is derived from the Brazilian E-Commerce Public Dataset by Olist . It provides a frozen reference cohort of 94,791 internally reconciled orders, 901 deterministic controlled instances, transaction-instance membership, evaluator-only oracle states, and state-specific monetary exposure. The benchmark represents four evidence states: `CONFIRMED`, `RECONSTRUCTED`, `CONFLICTING`, and `UNRESOLVED`. Controlled families cover missing evidence, hard conflicts, unique reconstruction, ambiguous reconstruction, duplicate evidence, and mixed corruption at 5%, 10%, 20%, 30%, and 40%. This release contains the reference oracle, controlled-instance definitions, compact membership index, exposure tables, data dictionary, provenance documentation, reconstruction code, validation code, manifests, schema catalog, and checksums. It contains no method predictions, comparative performance results, ablation studies, paper drafts, dashboards, or private Rahaskin data. Raw Olist CSV files are not redistributed and must be obtained from the original Kaggle source. Original source citation: Olist, & Sionek, A. (2018). Brazilian E-Commerce Public Dataset by Olist [Data set]. Kaggle. https://doi.org/10.34740/KAGGLE/DSV/195341 Official source: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/olistbr/brazilian-ecommerce License: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International (`CC BY-NC-SA 4.0`).
items.title: Olist Transactional Evidence Benchmark (OTEB)

items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly construct multi-agent workflows that decompose a complex task and assign specialist agents from a pool. However, building such a workflow well remains challenging: how finely to divide the task, which agent to trust with each subtask, and when to create a new specialist are all critical decisions a workflow constructor needs to settle up front. Thus, whether each subtask succeeds remains unknown until the workflow runs. Yet, improving a workflow is costly. Locating a fault usually requires a reference answer, a graded outcome, or a trained assessor, and the fix is applied to the whole workflow through re-execution, re-search, or retraining. We propose InFlowOp, which prices every decision in one label-free cost that weighs how well an agent's competence meets what a subtask demands against how much that agent takes to run. Before execution, InFlowOp bidirectionally determines the granularity of task decomposition and agent assignment following from the cost rather than from a fixed template. During execution, InFlowOp corrects a fault with the cheapest move via the same cost that serves the workflow both as it is built and as it runs. Facing the workflow-level evaluation challenge, we introduce Braid, a benchmark whose tasks require multi-agent coordination beyond single-agent capability. Across various domains and backbones, InFlowOp outperforms single agent baselines by up to $+11.97\%$, achieving $+9.64\%$ with in-flow optimization. Our project page: https://xhguo7.github.io/InFlowOp/.
items.title: Pay for the Fault, Not the Flow: Label-Free In-Flow Multi-Agent Workflow Optimization

items.summary: This dataset contains the derived summary resources supporting the manuscript Sequence-to-function models prioritize fine-mapped blood eQTLs in African American, Caribbean Hispanic, and Non-Hispanic White participants . The package includes the source tables for every main and supplementary figure and table, model-score summaries, fine-mapping benchmark tables, AUROC resampling summaries, the matched FILER functional-annotation enrichment analysis (inputs, results, and QC), the follow-up analyses that dissect the group difference (score anatomy, resampling, LD, allele frequency, label transfer, within-gene evaluation, annotation baselines), the model-first LD-reduced evaluation (configuration, results, and QC), the eQTLGen replication summary, and row-level prediction tables. The package is split into several archives; the top-level README and MANIFEST describe every file and how the archives fit together. No individual-level genotypes or sample identifiers are included. Analysis code for model scoring, summary analyses, and manuscript figure and table generation is available at https://github.com/Xinyu-Sun/s2f_snp_eqtl_analysis_code, commit b5a9e1270f431a82265d63f0b90ee17eabb9da6c. Version 2026-10-03.
items.title: Data package for evaluating sequence-to-function deep learning models for ancestry-stratified regulatory variant effect prediction

items.summary: This archive accompanies “Provenance-Aware Quality Control for Heterogeneous Bioactivity Data” by Xin Gao. It contains cached benchmark and fresh-target prediction tables, finite-pair curation summaries, cross-repository comparison materials, figure source tables, frozen manifests, and reproduction code for the non-hosted analyses. Run `python3 tools/recalculate_public_limited_companion.py` after extraction. The standard-library checker reconstructs retained confusion counts, Matthews correlation coefficients, pairwise disagreement summaries, and repository disagreement tiers without network access. This is a cached-statistics reproduction, not an end-to-end replay of every raw data pipeline or a hosted-model rerun. The archive deliberately excludes hosted-model MAPK14 per-item and aggregate outputs, Figure 8 source material, and raw payload, CIF, and run files because accepted-account redistribution terms were not retrieved. This is a conservative packaging decision and does not claim that the excluded material is necessarily restricted. Software is MIT-licensed; ChEMBL-derived adaptations retain applicable CC BY-SA obligations. BindingDB source dumps and publisher PDFs are not included.
items.title: Public-limited companion materials for Provenance-Aware Quality Control for Heterogeneous Bioactivity Data

items.summary: Code, partition manifests and per-image predictions supporting the audit and leakage-controlled re-evaluation of the 4,217-image Eye Disease Retinal Images collection.   Contents: the provenance and integrity audit; the manifests defining every evaluation arm image by image (image-level, patient-grouped, size-matched, source-matched, the common test set and the six leave-one-source-out splits); the training and evaluation code; stored per-image class probabilities for every run; the shortcut probes; and the visual adjudication verdicts for all 335 cross-label near-duplicate candidates.   The image collection itself is not redistributed here. It is available at https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/python16/eye-disease-retinal-images and the manifests reference it by relative path.
items.title: Acquisition source confounds a widely used retinal fundus benchmark: audit, partitions and per-run predictions

items.summary: Companion archive for the article Accuracy is not reliability: abstention-aware evaluation of large language models on bio-bibliographic claim verification in classical Islamic scholarship (Information Processing & Management, Elsevier, 2026, in press). Contents: the ISNAD benchmark (1,986 scored Turkish claims across five probe types) and the 360-item Turkish/Arabic GAL replication set with gold labels; freeze and exclusion manifests; 64,216 raw model-output records; blank expert-study forms with answer keys; and six analysis scripts with fixed seeds that regenerate the article's tables. Item-level expert responses are not released, at the annotator's request. Licences: code (analysis/) MIT; data (data/, human_studies/) CC BY 4.0. Factual information drawn from the TDV İslâm Ansiklopedisi and from Brockelmann's History of the Arabic Written Tradition; no rights are claimed over those works.
items.title: ISNAD: benchmark data and analysis code for "Accuracy is not reliability" (Information Processing & Management, 2026)

items.summary: This repository provides the reproducibility package accompanying the manuscript “Cross-fire transferability of four-year NBR-based spectral recovery after the 2021 wildfires in southwestern Türkiye”. The package contains the analysis-ready modelling sample, Google Earth Engine and Python analysis scripts, locked out-of-fold model predictions, model-selection records, sensitivity-analysis outputs, uncertainty and calibration results, derived tables and figures, random seeds, data dictionaries, provenance information, and supporting quality-control documentation. The study evaluates the transferability of four-year NBR-based spectral recovery across five 2021 wildfire complexes in southwestern Türkiye using outer leave-one-fire-out validation and spatially blocked inner cross-validation. The repository supports reproduction and auditing of the reported analyses. Source Sentinel-2, CORINE Land Cover, EFFIS, MODIS MCD64A1, and other third-party datasets remain subject to their original providers’ terms and licences. Spectral recovery reported in this study should not be interpreted as complete biomass, ecosystem, or restoration recovery.
items.title: Reproducibility package for cross-fire transferability of four-year NBR-based spectral recovery after the 2021 wildfires in southwestern Türkiye
